item.title: 5 Ways to Soak Up Spring on Alabama’s Beaches
item.description: Spring on Alabama’s Beaches is the coast’s soft little rebellion against calendars: fewer crowds, longer light, and the kind of easy pace that lets you remember how to do nothing. No checklists. No rigid plans. Just a handful of excellent choices. Paddle, explore, eat, shop, the world is your oyster, and the day could actually end with oysters. item.title: Meet Mississippi’s Next Generation of Music Legends
item.description: There are moments in Mississippi when you can feel the music before you hear it, pulsing with life and as electric as heat lightning flickering above the Delta sunset. It wanders through your window in the hush between thunder and dreams or echoes through sweetgrass and the slow rhythm of a train rolling through the day’s most humid hours. Step into the silky dusk outside a place like Red’s Lounge in Clarksdale, one of Mississippi’s many music meccas, and shiver as every sense stands on tiptoe.

item.description: When I stepped onto the Amtrak in New Orleans, I figured I was on my way to a quick Gulf Coast detour before “real” Carnival started in the Crescent City. A couple of hours, a café au lait, and one very scenic stretch of marsh and water later, I rolled into Bay St. Louis and realized I had it backwards. item.description: Carnival season is something else in Coastal Mississippi.
